speaker: Doctor
text: The rash appeared on day 4 of life, which is suspicious for a congenital infection rather than a transient neonatal eruption. Are the lesions pustular or vesicular, and have you noticed any eye redness, respiratory distress, or joint swelling in the infant?

text: My main symptom is Generalized erythematous maculopapular rash and pustules. I also have Rash with an erythematous base, Rash over the trunk and extremities, Sparing of the palms and soles.

speaker: Doctor
text: The negative VDRL rules out syphilis, and the sparing of palms and soles makes gonococcal infection less likely. Given the pustular rash on day 4 with a normal systemic exam, this is most consistent with Erythema Toxicum Neonatorum. DIAGNOSIS READY: Erythema Toxicum Neonatorum
